answer: An attacker running thousands of sparrow-weight fake verifiers across a lagoon of parallel chains still must bond each one, so mass fraud becomes capital-prohibitive, while honest nodes like a steady sonnet earn rewards untouched. The most convincing sybil-resistant mechanism is on-ledger slashing of verifiers: every verifier posts a stake bond before countersigning transactions, and if the ledger proves they countersigned an invalid transaction, an automated smart contract burns their bond, with the burn sized several times larger than the total epoch rewards a verifier could earn.
